references.text: The Lord is called 'God of the spirits of all flesh,' the same title Moses uses here when he asks for a new leader.
God breathed the breath of life into man, showing that He is the source of all spiritual life in every living being.
In God's hand is the soul of every living creature and the spirit of every human, confirming that He is 'the God of spirits.'
The spirit returns to God who gave it, demonstrating His sovereignty over all spirits.
The Lord says that the spirits and souls He has created come from Him, affirming His role as the God of spirits.
The Lord who stretched out the heavens and formed the human spirit within confirms His supremacy over all spirits.
God is called 'the Father of spirits,' corresponding to 'God of the spirits of all flesh' in the Old Testament.
God's answer to Moses' prayer: Joshua is appointed as leader over the congregation, fulfilling the request for a man over the assembly.
The Lord commands Moses to call Joshua and appoint him as leader, responding to Moses' prayer for a successor.
The Lord sends Samuel to anoint a new leader over Israel, an example of God raising up men over His people.
Jesus sees the crowds as sheep without a shepherd and tells the disciples to pray to the Lord of the harvest to send out workers, paralleling Moses' prayer for a leader over the congregation.
